narrative: Material PL1__M17AF202 shows erratic working-day demand (CV=0.51, mean 4,646 units/day) with no detectable trend and 97% non-zero days. Lead times are volatile (CV=0.47, mean 2.68 days), amplifying buffer requirements significantly. The combined lead-time demand sigma of 7,040 units requires a safety stock of 11,580 units at 95% service level — 3.4x the current SAP setting. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy with ROP=26,988 and OQ=31,199 is recommended; the incremental holding cost of $1,524/year is a cost-effective hedge against the high stockout risk inherent in the current underestimated safety stock.
warnings: Current SAP safety stock (3,393) is 241% below the model-recommended level (11,580) for 95% service level.

research_insights.selection_rationale: With 97.2% non-zero demand days and an erratic but continuously active pattern, a continuous-review reorder-point model is more appropriate than periodic-review. The EOQ batch (31,199) far exceeds the MOQ (1,045), making a fixed-quantity trigger straightforward to implement in SAP.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is not binding: SS+OQ=42,779 units vs. max 53,952 units, leaving 11,173 units of headroom. No capacity-driven service degradation is anticipated.
research_insights.escalation_flag: No MOQ-capacity infeasibility. However, the gap between current SAP safety stock (3,393) and recommended (11,580) is operationally significant and warrants urgent escalation to supply chain management for SAP master data correction.
